newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seen holding key Boeing meeting on July 4.
newsitem.headline: EU seen holding key Boeing meeting on July 4.

text.p: The European Commission will submit a draft decision on the merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp) to competition experts from the EU's 15 states on July 4, an industry source said on Wednesday.

The choice of the date -- a holiday in the United States to celebrate Independence Day -- was clearly seen as an attempt to avoid any information that leaks from the meeting affecting the companies' share price on the New York Stock Exchange.

It also showed that the Commission was leaving time to negotiate with the two American aircraft manufacturers in the event they fail to meet its competition concerns before it seeks the opinion of the national experts.
The Commission declined to confirm the date, but a source said it would be either July 3 or 4.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has until July 31 to submit a final decision on the $14 billion merger to the 20-member Commission. Merger decisions require a simple majority.

Experience with other high-profile mergers and acquisitions seen to harm fair competition in the EU's market has showed that serious negotiations only start after the advisory committee on concentrations has met and usually backed the conclusions reached by Van Miert's influential merger task-force.

The draft decision and the opinion of the committee are not made public. But because the case becomes available to a larger audience -- instead of being restricted to the secretive task force -- information is sometimes easier to obtain.
Boeing has shown little desire to address the Commission's concerns, contesting the EU's preliminary views that its acquisition of McDonnell Douglas would affect the Union.

Boeing also denies that the EU has jurisdiction to force it to scrap exclusive supply deals with AMR's American Airlines and Delta Air Lines. A third contract was announced on Tuesday by Continental Airlines.
